# PR #4961: Patch: the Duos AI weighs the teammate's whole hand before it passes

Closes #4932

The Duos AI's two pass scores now keep the teammate's highest-valued cards when the teammate has more plays than fit in the 8-play limit, instead of the first 8 in hand order. The limit itself is still 8 engine steps per score. The new tests show the fix works, the Duos gate is green, and the paired comparison against the base build was inconclusive: the change rarely comes up in gate games.

## What changed

- **`crates/ai/src/duos.rs`**: a new helper, `best_valued_plays(state, mate, plays, limit)`.
  - If the list fits in `limit`, it is returned unchanged, in its original order.
  - If it doesn't fit, the helper keeps the first listed play of each card, ordered by `hand_card_value` on the teammate's probe, highest first. Ties keep list order (the sort is stable, on `total_cmp`). A play of a card not in hand, such as a graveyard play (R454), goes last.
  - It reads the hand as it is, at any size (R1143), and adds no engine step.
- **`pass_score`** (the teammate's follow-up with the passed card): the passed card's own plays still come first. The teammate's other plays now fill the room that leaves through `best_valued_plays`.
- **`mate_baseline`** (the teammate's best play without the pass): the first play of each card goes through `best_valued_plays` with the full limit of 8, instead of `.take(8)`.
- **`crates/ai/src/config.rs`**: `DUOS_PASS_MAX_FOLLOWUPS` stays 8. Its doc comment now describes the ordering and records the measured screen.
- **Spec**:
  - New ruling `spec/rulings/R4932000.md` (the first number of issue #4932's block) and its paragraph in `spec/pending/4932.md`.
  - R1127000's title and one clause, and one clause of R1723000, now link it.
  - One sentence added to §13.7's **Passing.** bullet, and to the `duos_passes` bullet in `crates/ai/README.md`.
- **`crates/ai/tests/ai/duos.rs`**: three `r4932000_…` scene tests and a `crowded_trade_state` helper:
  1. **Full hand**: with hand sizes of 10, 12 and 14 (`HAND_CAP`, `HAND_CAP + 2`, `HAND_CAP_MAX`), the teammate holds one-drops with its own BIG last, past the old cut. The pass must match the case where BIG is held alone (no pass), while one-drops alone still get the pass.
  2. **Below the limit, unchanged**: 8 cards, with hand sizes of 9, 10 and 14.
  3. **The room in `pass_score`**: BIG's five lanes leave room for three of the teammate's plays. With the teammate's hand as `[STAB, BIG]`, the Stab's second listed play (a win) used to fill that room and be credited to the pass.

## How I tested it

- **Before the fix**, `cargo test -p jackioh-ai --test ai r4932000` failed as intended:
  - test 1 at `cap 10: A2's own BIG past the bound`;
  - test 3 on `["core-070", "core-025"]` (`[STAB, BIG]`);
  - test 2 passed.
- **After the fix**, all three pass.
- **Each test checks its own call site**: with only `mate_baseline` fixed (the `pass_score` change reverted), test 3 fails and test 1 passes.
- `cargo test -p jackioh-ai`: all pass (72 unit tests, 1087 in `ai`, 105 in `ai_slow`). The 15 ignored in `ai_slow` were already marked daily.
- `cargo clippy -p jackioh-ai --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo jackioh spec check` (`2603 rulings … ok`) are all green.
- `cargo jackioh gate --duos` (smoke): exit 0. Random 20/20, greedy 18/20, with no rejections, fallbacks or panics.
- **Paired comparison**: `gate --duos --games 40`, with the control binary built before any edit and the candidate after, on the same seeds. The bar was fixed in the plan before the run: keep if down − up ≤ 2·√decided; inconclusive below R4319000's 20 decided games.

  | | Random (won of 40) | Greedy (won of 40) |
  |---|---|---|
  | Control | 39 | 36 |
  | Candidate | 39 | 36 |

  - Both runs exited 0.
  - 1 of 80 games played differently (greedy seed 38: both won, in 206 vs 158 actions). Up 0, down 0, decided 0.
  - So the result is **inconclusive** and the change is kept, with the scene tests settling it, as the plan's bar says.
- `cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims` printed `Internal`, but only because nothing is committed yet. An AI-only change needs no patch fragment, since claims cover cards that play differently.
- I did not run the workspace-wide test suite; the harness runs it next.

## Decisions the issue left open

- **The limit stays 8.** I read "should read an arbitrary value" as "read the hand as it stands and assume no hand size". I rejected raising the limit to the hand's size: those steps are unmeasured and the issue asks for no new ones.
- **Ordering only when the list doesn't fit.** A list that fits is scored exactly as before. I rejected always sorting, which would change scores that are already complete.
- **When ordering, one play per card.** When the list doesn't fit, each card gets its first play rather than all its lanes and targets, so one Unit's five lanes can't fill all the room. I rejected filling leftover room with more plays in list order: the baseline only ever sees first plays, so this would credit the pass with plays the baseline never weighs. Test 3 is that case.
- **`own_use_gain` and `pass_gain`'s card plays are unchanged.** Each lists one card's plays, which all have the same hand value, so ordering would do nothing.
- **The ruling's `cards` field** lists `§13.7, R1127000, R1723000`, not just `§13.7`, since it amends both rulings.

## Worth a second look

- The ordering value is mostly the card's cost. The best play is still chosen by real engine steps, just over a better 8.
- `pass_score` also changes for small hands whenever the other plays don't fit the room. A passed Unit alone takes 5 of the 8. Every existing test still passes.
- **Possible follow-up issue, not in this change.** The baseline only weighs each card's first listed play, and a targeted card lists targets on its own side first. So the fix covers a ninth-card Unit but not, for example, a ninth-card burn spell. I didn't test this case myself.

# #4932: Patch: the Duos AI weighs the teammate's whole hand before it passes
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

In Duos games against the AI team, the AI may pass a card to its teammate when its own turn ends. To decide, it scores what the teammate could do with the card and what the teammate's best play without it is. Both scores stop after 8 candidate plays, cut in engine list order, not by value. A teammate holding 9-10 cards (the hand cap is 10) therefore has some cards cut before anything is scored, so the AI can pass a card the teammate cannot use, or keep one the teammate needed, purely because the good play sat past the cut. Players see this as the AI team passing badly in long Duos games with full hands.

## Why

`pass_score` (`crates/ai/src/duos.rs:426-461`) chains the passed card's own plays first, then the teammate's other plays in `legal_actions` order, and takes `DUOS_PASS_MAX_FOLLOWUPS` (8, `crates/ai/src/config.rs:133`); `mate_baseline` (`crates/ai/src/duos.rs:508-521`) takes the first `Play` of each of at most 8 hand cards. With `HAND_CAP` 10 (`crates/engine/src/config.rs:57`), a full teammate hand leaves two cards (and in `pass_score`, every play past the eighth) unweighed. Hand order is arrival order, not value order, so the cut is arbitrary: a removal or lethal sitting ninth in the list never enters either side of the comparison. No open issue covers this (#4795 is the pass nonce bug, a different mechanism), and none of the rejected suggestions does (#4533 is about the 1v1 reply spending Credits and trading dead Tradables). The node cost need not move: the same 8 engine steps, chosen better.

## Proposal

Order the teammate's candidate first-plays by a free static score (hand value) before taking the 8 in `pass_score` and `mate_baseline` (and the same card's variants in `own_use_gain`), so the bound keeps the best 8 instead of the first 8. Add scene tests with a 10-card teammate hand where the best follow-up sits past the old cut: the pass decision must match full-hand scoring. Screen on the Duos gate series with candidate and control builds on the same frozen seeds (same deals), keeping the change only on a paired comparison decided in advance that shows no regression and on scene tests carrying the behavior.

## Where it lands

- `crates/ai/src/duos.rs` (`pass_score`, `mate_baseline`, `own_use_gain` ordering; no new nodes)
- `crates/ai/src/config.rs` (comment on `DUOS_PASS_MAX_FOLLOWUPS` recording the screen)
- `crates/ai/tests/ai/duos.rs` (scene tests: full-hand pass choice with 9-10 cards)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Scene test fails without the fix (pass differs from full-hand scoring when the best play is past the cut) and passes with it; a 10-card hand case and a below-the-bound case that is unchanged.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-ai` and `cargo clippy -p jackioh-ai --all-targets -- -D warnings` green.
- [ ] `cargo jackioh gate --duos` smoke green with the candidate (no fallback, refusal or panic, which already fails the gate).
- [ ] Candidate-versus-control paired comparison on the same duos-gate seeds, size and keep bar decided in advance, shows no regression.
- [ ] Per-pass engine-step count unchanged (still at most 8 takes per scoring site) unless a measured raise is part of the kept change.

## Size and risks

Small (ordering plus tests); measurement is the duos gate plus a paired same-seed comparison, both cheap next to a 400-game screen. Risk is that static ordering mis-ranks versus engine-step scoring; contained because the max is still taken over real engine steps, only over a better 8, and the gate plus scene tests hold behavior.

   fn best_valued_plays(state: &GameState, mate: PlayerId, plays: Vec<ActionBody>, limit: usize) -> Vec<ActionBody> {

               let value = worth(instance_id);
               Some((value, action))
           })
           .collect();
       // A stable sort: equal values keep list order.
       firsts.sort_by(|a, b| b.0.total_cmp(&a.0));
       firsts.into_iter().take(limit).map(|(_, action)| action).collect()
   }

    let mut hand = vec![ONE_DROP; held - usize::from(last.is_some())];
